aws-clf-c02-t1.2-03.statement: Automatically recovering from failure is a design principle of the performance efficiency pillar.
aws-clf-c02-t1.2-03.explanation: Automatically recovering from failure is a reliability design principle, alongside testing recovery procedures and scaling horizontally.
aws-clf-c02-t1.2-03.misconception: Mixing up the reliability and performance efficiency pillars.

aws-clf-c02-t1.4-12.statement: AWS cost optimization guidance recommends measuring a workload's business output alongside its cost.
aws-clf-c02-t1.4-12.explanation: The "measure overall efficiency" design principle ties spending to business output, so teams can see the gains from increasing output and reducing cost.

aws-clf-c02-t2.1-04.reason: strawman, replaced with a new card
aws-clf-c02-t2.1-04.statement: In the shared responsibility model, security "of" the cloud is the customer's responsibility.
aws-clf-c02-t2.1-04.explanation: Security of the cloud is the AWS side of the model. The customer side is security in the cloud.
aws-clf-c02-t2.1-04.misconception: Swapping "security of the cloud" (AWS) with "security in the cloud" (customer).

aws-clf-c02-t2.2-07.statement: AWS Config rules prevent noncompliant resources from being created.
aws-clf-c02-t2.2-07.explanation: AWS Config evaluates resource configurations and flags noncompliant resources. Blocking an action takes a preventive control, such as an IAM policy.
aws-clf-c02-t2.2-07.misconception: Confusing compliance assessment with preventive enforcement.

source.title: Components of an AWS Config Rule

aws-clf-c02-t3.1-06.statement: An on-premises deployment that uses virtualization provides most of the benefits of cloud computing.
aws-clf-c02-t3.1-06.explanation: AWS says on-premises deployment with virtualization, sometimes called private cloud, lacks many of the benefits of cloud computing and is mostly the same as legacy IT.
aws-clf-c02-t3.1-06.misconception: Assuming virtualization on its own delivers the benefits of cloud computing.

source.title: Types of cloud computing - Overview of Amazon Web Services
